ig_caption:
Back to chess after a few weeks away, and your rating is jumping about? That's normal.

First, you're rusty, not worse. Time away dulls the small habits: checking threats, counting pieces, using your clock. They come back much faster than they took to learn.

Second, points can move faster. Most chess sites use a rating system that becomes less sure of your rating while you're away, so your first games back can move it more than usual, up or down.

So warm up with a few puzzles or unrated games, start with slower games before quick ones, and give it a couple of weeks before you judge your graph.

slides.title: Back after a break?
slides.sub: WHAT HAPPENS WHEN YOU COME BACK

slides.title: Rusty, not worse
slides.body: Time away dulls the small habits: checking threats, counting pieces, watching your clock. A few poor games after a break are normal.
slides.note: Habits come back much faster than they took to learn.

slides.title: Points move faster
slides.body: Most chess sites use a rating system that grows less sure of your rating while you're away. So your first games back can move it more than usual, up or down.
slides.note: Big swings early on are the system catching up, not a verdict on you.

slides.title: Warm up first
slides.body: Before your first rated game back, solve a few puzzles or play an unrated game or two. Let your eyes get used to the board again.
slides.note: Ten quiet minutes can save a lot of points.

slides.title: Start slower
slides.body: Quick games punish rusty habits the most. Play a few longer games first, so you have time to check each move properly.
slides.note: Go back to your favourite speed once you feel at home again.

slides.title: Judge it in a fortnight
slides.body: Your first week back says more about the break than about your chess. Look at your graph after a couple of weeks of steady play.
slides.note: A dip after time away is a dent, not a drop in level.
